svg.title: First Take the Log Out
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 6 panels. Panel 1 (Matthew 7:3): Jesus seated on a hillside, teaching two seated disciples. Caption: "Jesus sits and teaches." Jesus says: "Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but do not notice the log that is in your own eye?" Panel 2 (Luke 6:41-42): a disciple with an enormous roof beam jutting from his eye and off the edge of the panel, leaning in to reach for a tiny speck in the eye of a seated brother; the beam passes over the brother's head. Caption: "The picture He paints:". A disciple says: "Brother, let me take out the speck that is in your eye,". Note: "His own overstatement, drawn as He says it." Panel 3 (Matthew 7:5): Jesus, in a medium shot, speaking. Caption: "Jesus says:". Jesus says: "You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye,". Panel 4 (Matthew 7:5): the beam lying on the ground; the disciple kneels close to his seated brother and reaches gently for the speck in his eye. Caption: "The beam set down." Jesus says: "and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye." Panel 5 (2 Samuel 12:1-7), a flashback: Nathan standing behind King David, pointing at him, while David points away in anger at the man in the story, a long beam jutting from David's eye. Caption: "Long before: Nathan's story of the stolen lamb." David says: "the man who has done this deserves to die". Nathan says: "You are the man!" Panel 6 (Psalm 51:1, 13): David kneeling in prayer, the beam lying on the floor beside him. Caption: "David's psalm, "when Nathan the prophet went to him."" David says: "Then I will teach transgressors your ways". The point: God alone judges, and He measures you with your own measure. Let Him take the log out of your eye first; then you will see clearly to help your brother, gently, as one forgiven (Matthew 7:2, 5; Psalm 51:13).
svg.text: A carpenter's joke, and a king who did not see his own

text.tspan: Why do you see the speck
that is in your own eye?

svg.text: God alone judges, and He measures you with your own measure. Let Him
take the log out of your eye first; then you will see clearly to help
your brother, gently, as one forgiven (Matthew 7:2, 5; Psalm 51:13).
Panels 2 and 5 draw Jesus' overstatement as He says it; 2 Samuel 12
has no beam. The brother in Jesus' picture has no recorded words.
